title: Careers and Pathways in Digital Technology

pages.c04-p01: Explain why digital skills are needed in almost every job, not only in 'computer jobs'
pages.c04-p02: Describe what software developers, cyber security analysts and data scientists do day to day
pages.c04-p03: Describe what network and cloud engineers, web, UX and games designers, and IT support technicians do, and link each career area to KS3 Digital Technology
pages.c04-p04: Describe the tech sector in Northern Ireland, the types of employer and how hybrid and remote working affect where you can work
pages.c04-p05: Describe the qualification route from KS3 through GCSE and A level Digital Technology (CCEA) and what each stage involves
pages.c04-p06: Compare university degrees with apprenticeships, including ApprenticeshipsNI and Higher Level Apprenticeships in Northern Ireland
pages.c04-p07: Describe the skills employers look for, such as problem solving, teamwork, communication and resilience, and show evidence of them using STAR
pages.c04-p08: Explain how to build a portfolio of digital work through projects, clubs, competitions and programmes such as TechFirst
pages.c04-p09: Explain how your digital footprint and online reputation can affect your future, and how to behave professionally online
pages.c04-p10: Write a skills-based CV and plan a personal statement for a tech course or job
pages.c04-p11: Explain why diversity matters in technology and challenge myths and stereotypes about who 'does' computing
pages.c04-p12: Create a personal careers plan with SMART targets for your next steps

q.q: Which statement best describes digital skills?
o: The ability to repair broken computer hardware only
The abilities to use, understand and create with digital technology
The ability to type quickly without looking at the keys
The qualifications needed to become a programmer
q.why: Digital skills range from using software confidently to creating content and writing code.

q.q: What is a transferable skill?
o: A skill that can be used in many different jobs or subjects
A skill that only one particular job needs
A skill copied from a colleague's work
A qualification that is accepted in other countries
q.why: Skills such as problem solving move with you from one job to another.

q.q: What is automation?
o: People checking every computer task by hand
Moving data from one computer to another by email
Replacing all workers with robots that need no people
Computers and machines doing tasks that people once did by hand
q.why: Automation takes over repetitive tasks, but people are still needed to set up and check the systems.

q.q: A nurse updates patient notes on a tablet. What does this show?
o: Nurses are really a type of IT support technician
Health trusts no longer use any paper
Digital skills matter in jobs that are not computer jobs
Automation has replaced the nurse's job
q.why: Health is not a tech job, but it relies on digital systems such as electronic patient records.

q.q: A café worker enters weekly sales into a spreadsheet. Which digital skill is she mainly using?
o: Network engineering
Handling data
Cyber security testing
Programming in Python
q.why: Recording and organising sales figures is handling data.

q.q: Why are people still needed when a business uses automation?
o: To set up, check and improve the automated systems
Because automated systems never make any errors
Because the law bans computers from working alone
To do the same tasks again by hand as a backup
q.why: Automated systems must be designed, monitored and improved by people.

q.q: Which reason best explains why every worker needs basic cyber security habits?
o: Every worker will eventually become a security analyst
Cyber security habits make computers run faster
Workers must be able to hack into rival companies
One careless click on a phishing email can harm everyone
q.why: Attackers often get in through ordinary staff, so everyone needs safe habits.

q.q: Debugging a program in class mainly builds which transferable skill?
o: Customer service
Graphic design
Problem solving
Public speaking
q.why: Finding and fixing errors means breaking a problem down and testing solutions.

q.q: Which job title is another name for a software developer?
o: Network technician
Software engineer
Data analyst
UX researcher
q.why: Software developers are also called programmers or software engineers.

q.q: What is a bug?
o: An error in a program that makes it go wrong
A small program that speeds up a computer
A feature requested by a user
A message sent between developers
q.why: Developers test code to find and fix bugs.

q.q: Which is a correctly written user story?
o: The app must have a homework page with a blue button at the top
Pupils forget homework so the app should fix the problem somehow
As a developer, I will write the homework page in Python today
As a pupil, I want to see my homework on my phone so that I don't forget it
q.why: User stories follow the pattern: As a [user], I want [something] so that [reason].

q.q: What is a stand-up meeting in a software team?
o: A meeting where developers present to customers
An interview for a new software developer
A short daily meeting to agree what everyone will work on
A meeting held only when a program has failed
q.why: Many teams start each day with a quick stand-up.

q.q: Which task is most typical of a cyber security analyst?
o: Designing the levels of a new mobile game
Investigating a login from an unusual country at 3 am
Interviewing users about a confusing menu
Cleaning duplicate rows from a sales dataset
q.why: Analysts watch for suspicious activity and respond to attacks.

q.q: Which task is most typical of a data scientist?
o: Using past passenger data to predict bus numbers
Fixing a printer that will not connect
Testing a website on a screen reader
Running new fibre cables between offices
q.why: Finding patterns in data to make predictions is data science.

q.q: Software development is described as a cycle. Which order is right?
o: Develop, release, plan, then stop
Test, plan, develop, then finish
Plan, release, test, then develop
Plan, develop, test, refine, then plan again
q.why: Teams keep planning, building, testing and refining in a cycle.

q.q: A developer uses a generative AI tool to write a function. What is the best practice?
o: Use it without changes because AI code is always correct
Delete it because AI code can never be used at work
Review and test the code because AI can be confidently wrong
Ask the AI tool to confirm it is correct and move on
q.why: The developer is responsible for the code, so it must be checked and tested.

q.q: A data scientist checks whether an AI model treats different groups of people fairly. What are they checking for?
o: Encryption
Bias
Bandwidth
Syntax
q.why: Unfair results from an AI model are called bias.

q.q: What does UX stand for?
o: User experience
User exchange
Universal export
Unified extension
q.why: UX designers focus on the experience of the people using a product.

q.q: What is cloud computing?
o: Storing data only on a USB stick you carry
Running software on your own laptop with no internet
Sending data through the air using weather satellites and clouds
Storing data and running software on servers over the internet
q.why: Cloud services run in data centres, not on your own device.

q.q: Which job is a common first job in tech, often leading on to networking or cyber security?
o: Data scientist
Lead games designer
IT support technician
Penetration tester
q.why: IT support builds broad experience of systems and users.

q.q: What does user-centred design mean?
o: Designing what the developer personally likes best
Designing around who the product is for and what they need
Designing so the product looks as modern as possible
Designing first and asking users after release only
q.why: User-centred design asks who a product is for, not just whether it works.

q.q: Which guidelines help designers make websites accessible?
o: WCAG
HTTPS
UCAS
GDPR
q.why: The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines help make products usable by everyone.

q.q: Why do cloud and network engineers need to think about sustainability?
o: Cloud servers run without any electricity at all
Network cables are made entirely from recycled paper
Laws ban data centres from using renewable energy
Data centres use a lot of electricity and water for cooling
q.why: Running and cooling data centres has an environmental cost.

q.q: A beautiful app cannot be read by a screen reader. What is the best judgement?
o: It has excellent UX because it looks attractive
It is fine because few people use screen readers
It has poor user experience because some users cannot use it
It is a cyber security problem, not a design one
q.why: UX is about how well people can use a product, not only how it looks.

q.q: Which KS3 idea links most directly to cyber security jobs?
o: Writing user stories
Encryption and HTTPS
Choosing chart types
Designing game levels
q.why: Encryption protects data as it travels and is central to cyber security.

q.q: Which NI city is best known for its software and cyber security industry?
o: Belfast
Armagh
Enniskillen
Lisburn
q.why: About 85% of NI cyber security firms were based in Belfast in 2023.

q.q: About how many cyber security firms were there in Northern Ireland in 2023?
q.why: The 2023 Northern Ireland Cybersecurity Snapshot counted 124 firms.

q.q: About how many people worked in NI cyber security in 2023?
o: About 275
About 27,500
About 2,750
About 750
q.why: The 2023 snapshot reported about 2,750 people.

q.q: What is CSIT at Queen's University Belfast?
o: A company that builds video games
A major cyber security research centre
A further education college in Belfast
The exam board for GCSE Digital Technology
q.why: CSIT is the Centre for Secure Information Technologies.

q.q: What is hybrid working?
o: Splitting the working week between the office and home
Working for two different companies at once
Working only at weekends and in the evenings
Working from home every single day
q.why: Hybrid mixes office days and home days.

q.q: Which employer is NOT a tech company but still employs network engineers and security staff?
o: A cyber security firm
A software start-up
An app development company
A health trust
q.why: Hospitals need secure, reliable systems too.

q.q: Niall lives in Fermanagh and gets a hybrid job with a Belfast company. Which is the best advantage?
o: He never needs an internet connection at home
He will learn faster by never seeing colleagues
He can stay in Fermanagh and travel only on some days
He no longer needs to communicate with his team
q.why: Hybrid working reduces travel and widens where you can live.

q.q: Why might an IT support technician be less likely to work fully remotely?
o: IT support work is not allowed to be done from home
They often need to be on site to handle the actual equipment
They do not use computers in their job
Remote working is only for company directors
q.why: Fixing hardware and setting up devices often needs someone in person.

q.q: Why should you treat figures such as '124 cyber firms' with some care when making choices?
o: They are a snapshot from one year and change over time
They were invented by a computer game
They count firms in the Republic of Ireland only
They are secret and should not be shared
q.why: Sector figures change each year, so check up-to-date information.

q.q: Which CCEA GCSE Digital Technology route do ERGS pupils follow?
o: Route A: Multimedia
Route C: Networking
Route B: Multimedia
Route B: Programming
q.why: ERGS follows Route B: Programming, made up of Units 1, 4 and 5.

q.q: What is the title of GCSE Unit 4?
o: Digital Development Practice
Digital Authoring Concepts
Digital Development Concepts
Fundamentals of Digital Technology
q.why: Unit 4 is Digital Development Concepts, a written exam on programming.

q.q: How is Unit 5: Digital Development Practice assessed?
o: A 1 hour written exam
Controlled assessment in school
A 1 hour 30 minute written exam
An oral interview with CCEA
q.why: Unit 5 is a controlled assessment where you build a programmed solution.

q.q: What is the weighting of Unit 4 in the Route B GCSE?
q.why: Unit 1 is 30%, Unit 4 is 40% and Unit 5 is 30%.

q.q: Which A level Digital Technology unit is worth 40% of the A level?
o: AS 1: Approaches to Systems Development
A2 2: Application Development
AS 2: Fundamentals of Digital Technology
A2 1: Information Systems
q.why: A2 1 is a 2 hour 30 minute exam worth 40%.

q.q: A pupil scores 60% of the marks in Unit 5. How many percentage points of the whole GCSE is that?
q.why: Unit 5 is worth 30%, and 0.6 x 30 = 18.

q.q: A pupil scores 75% in Unit 4. How many percentage points of the GCSE has Unit 4 given them?
q.why: Unit 4 is worth 40%, and 0.75 x 40 = 30.

q.q: What qualification level is a bachelor's degree?
o: Level 6
Level 3
Level 5
Level 7
q.why: A levels are level 3, a foundation degree level 5, a bachelor's degree level 6 and a master's level 7.

q.q: What is an apprenticeship?
o: A full-time university course with no job
An unpaid week of work experience
A course you must finish before GCSEs
A paid job that includes training towards a qualification
q.why: Apprentices work for an employer and train at the same time.

q.q: Which levels does ApprenticeshipsNI cover?
o: Levels 4 to 7
Levels 1 and 2
Levels 2 and 3
Levels 5 and 6
q.why: ApprenticeshipsNI is at levels 2 and 3; Higher Level Apprenticeships cover 4 to 7.

q.q: Which levels do Higher Level Apprenticeships in NI cover?
o: Levels 2 and 3
Levels 4 to 7
Levels 3 to 5
Level 6 only
q.why: HLAs run from foundation degree level up to master's level.

q.q: At least how many hours a week must an NI apprentice work, including training?
q.why: Apprentices must work at least 21 hours a week.

q.q: In NI, what is the closest equivalent to an English degree apprenticeship?
o: An ApprenticeshipsNI course at level 3
A GCSE taken through a college
A level 4 HND studied full time
A Higher Level Apprenticeship at level 6
q.why: Level 6 is bachelor's degree level.

q.q: Which is an advantage of a Higher Level Apprenticeship over a full-time degree?
o: You never need to study or sit assessments
It always takes less than one year to finish
You are paid and do not pay higher education tuition fees
You do not need an employer to take you on
q.why: HLAs combine a wage with study, without HE tuition fees.

q.q: Which college with a campus in Enniskillen offers Higher Level Apprenticeships in computing?
o: Belfast Met
South West College
Northern Regional College
Queen's University Belfast
q.why: South West College has campuses including Enniskillen.

q.q: Which statement about apprenticeships is a myth?
o: Apprenticeships are only for people who missed out on university
Apprentices are paid while they train
Apprenticeships in NI can go right up to master's level
Apprentices gain work experience and a qualification
q.why: HLAs go up to level 7 and places can be very competitive.

q.q: What are soft skills?
o: Skills used only in software development
Skills that are easy and not valued by employers
Technical skills such as writing Python code
Personal skills that help you work well with others
q.why: Communication, teamwork and resilience are soft skills.

q.q: What does STAR stand for?
o: Skill, Talent, Ability, Reward
Start, Test, Adjust, Repeat
Situation, Task, Action, Result
Situation, Target, Answer, Review
q.why: STAR helps you structure evidence of a skill.

q.q: What is resilience?
o: Never making a mistake in any piece of work
Keeping going when things go wrong and learning from it
Working faster than everyone else in the team
Refusing to change your mind about anything
q.why: Resilience is bouncing back from setbacks.

q.q: Which statement gives the strongest evidence of communication skills?
o: I presented our app to Year 8 and answered questions
I am a really good communicator
I talk to lots of people every day
My friends always say that I am very easy to talk to
q.why: A specific example with an outcome is real evidence.

q.q: In the Action step of STAR, what should you mainly describe?
o: What the whole team did together
What your teacher asked you to do
What the final mark for the project was
What you personally did
q.why: Employers want to know your part, so say 'I'.

q.q: A pupil's code fails testing three times, and each time she logs the fault and fixes it. Which two skills does this best show?
o: Creativity and public speaking
Teamwork and leadership
Resilience and problem solving
Organisation and customer service
q.why: Persisting through failure and fixing faults shows resilience and problem solving.

q.q: Which part of a STAR answer is: 'The site was finished on time and I learned to test early'?
o: Situation
Result
Task
Action
q.why: The Result says what happened and what you learned.

q.q: Which is the best reason to keep a skills log?
o: You build up real examples to use in applications later
It replaces the need for any qualifications
Employers ask to see every log entry you write
It makes your school projects count for more marks
q.why: Writing STAR examples as you go gives you evidence for CVs and interviews.

q.q: What is a portfolio?
o: A list of your exam grades and school reports
A folder of certificates for attendance only
A summary of every lesson you have attended
A collection of your best work that shows what you can do
q.why: A portfolio proves your skills with real work.

q.q: Which programme replaced CyberFirst in 2026?
o: Code Club
Bebras
TechFirst
CoderDojo
q.why: CyberFirst became part of the larger TechFirst programme.

q.q: Which organisation leads the cyber pathway within TechFirst?
o: The Raspberry Pi Foundation
The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)
The exam board CCEA
The university admissions service UCAS
q.why: The NCSC ran CyberFirst and now leads TechFirst's cyber pathway.

q.q: Which year group in Northern Ireland is the TechFirst Girls Competition aimed at?
o: Year 9
Year 8
Year 11
Year 13
q.why: In NI it is for Year 9; in England and Wales, Year 8.

q.q: What is the UK Bebras Challenge?
o: A hackathon held only for university students
A coding club that meets every Saturday
A cyber security qualification for adults
A computational thinking challenge held each November
q.why: Bebras is a free problem-solving challenge run by the Raspberry Pi Foundation.

q.q: What is a Capture the Flag competition?
o: An outdoor team game organised by sports clubs
An illegal attempt to break into a real website
A legal cyber contest where you solve puzzles to find flags
A contest to design a flag for a tech company
q.why: CTFs give safe, legal cyber puzzles.

q.q: What is a hackathon?
o: An attack on a company's network by criminals
A short event where teams build a solution to a challenge
A long online course on ethical hacking
A test of how quickly you can type code
q.why: Hackathons usually last a day or a weekend.

q.q: Which is the best description of a portfolio piece?
o: The problem, who it was for, what I did and what I improved
The programming language and the date only
A screenshot with no explanation at all
A list of everyone who helped, with their grades
q.why: Good descriptions explain problem, users, your actions and refinements.

q.q: A pupil adds AI-generated code to his portfolio as his own work. What is the main problem?
o: AI code always contains viruses
Portfolios must not include any code
It will make the portfolio too long
It is dishonest and does not show his real skills
q.why: Always credit sources and only claim your own work.

q.q: What is a digital footprint?
o: The physical size of your computer
A fingerprint used to unlock a phone
The trail of data you leave online
The number of devices you own
q.why: Posts, likes, comments and tags all add to it.

q.q: What is online reputation?
o: The number of followers you have
What people think of you from what they find online
The privacy settings on your social media accounts
The speed of your home internet
q.why: Your reputation is formed from your footprint.

q.q: Which email address is most professional for an apprenticeship application?
o: niamh.oneill@...
niamhrocks2011@...
xxgamerqueenxx@...
lazysunday99@...
q.why: An address based on your name looks professional.

q.q: Why is deleting an embarrassing post not always enough?
o: Deleted posts reappear automatically after a month
Only the police are allowed to delete posts
Deleting a post makes it visible to everyone
Others may already have screenshotted or shared it
q.why: Once posted, content can be copied.

q.q: Which would build a positive online reputation?
o: Posting jokes that mock a classmate
Arguing with strangers in comments
Sharing a website you built for a local club
Sharing a friend's photo without asking
q.why: Showing your work builds a positive footprint.

q.q: What does professionalism mean?
o: Wearing a suit whenever you go online
Behaving reliably, respectfully and appropriately at work
Only using the internet for school work
Having a job title that includes 'professional'
q.why: Professional behaviour online includes polite messages and respecting others.

q.q: Which message to a teacher is most professional?
o: Hello Mr Butler, could you tell me where this week's homework is? Thank you, Aoife.
hey sir wheres the homework for this week, need it asap
HOMEWORK??? where is it, I cant find it anywhere on the site
yo sir need the hw asap thx, its due tomorrow i think lol
q.why: Polite greeting, clear request and sign-off.

q.q: According to the think-first check, which question should you ask before posting?
o: How many likes will this get in an hour?
Is my phone battery high enough to post?
Will this post go viral by the morning?
Would I be happy for a future employer to see this?
q.why: Imagine it on a screen at a job interview.

q.q: Eoin's gaming video shows him swearing at players. What should he do before applying for a job?
o: Leave it, because employers never search names
Post more videos so it is harder to find
Make it private or delete it, and check what else is public
Change his name so nobody can find him
q.why: Taking control of his footprint reduces the risk of a bad impression.

q.q: What is a CV?
o: A letter from a teacher about your character
A short summary of your skills, education and experience
A list of every lesson you have ever had
A form that only universities ask for
q.why: CV stands for curriculum vitae.

q.q: What does a skills-based CV put first?
o: Your skills, each backed by evidence
A full list of your previous jobs
Your home address and date of birth
Your hobbies and favourite films
q.why: It suits young people with little work history.

q.q: How long should a CV usually be?
o: At least five pages
Exactly one line
As long as possible
No more than two pages
q.why: Employers want a short, clear summary.

q.q: Which contact details are sensible on a teenager's CV?
o: Full address, date of birth and bank details
Social media passwords and home address
Name, phone number, professional email and town
Nickname, gaming username and school locker number
q.why: Your town is enough; keep personal details safe.

q.q: How many questions does the UCAS personal statement ask for courses from 2026?
o: One
Three
Two
Five
q.why: UCAS asks three questions in 4,000 characters in total.

q.q: A pupil writes answers of 1,500, 1,300 and 900 characters. How many characters are left from the UCAS limit?
Answers of 1,600, 1,500 and 1,100 characters are written. What is the problem?
o: They total 4,200, which is 200 under the limit
They total 3,200, which leaves 800 to spare
They total 4,000, which is exactly the limit
They total 4,200, which is 200 over the limit

q.q: Which is the best 'Key skills' entry for a CV?
o: IT skills: very good with all computers
Spreadsheets: I am excellent at them
Spreadsheets: built a tuck shop tracker with charts
Computers: I use them a lot at home for games and videos
q.why: It names a skill and gives specific evidence.

q.q: What should you do before naming a teacher as a referee?
o: Write the reference yourself
Ask the teacher's permission
Include their home phone number
Tell them after you have applied
q.why: Always ask before naming someone.

q.q: What is a stereotype?
o: A fixed, over-simple idea about what a group is like
A fact proven by careful research
A type of audio equipment
A role model who inspires people in a particular job
q.why: Stereotypes put people off careers they might love.

q.q: About what percentage of UK IT specialists were women in 2025?
q.why: BCS reported about 22%, roughly one in five.

q.q: A team of 200 IT specialists matched the UK figure of 22% women. How many women would there be?
Who wrote what is often called the first published computer program?
o: Grace Hopper
Ada Lovelace
Katherine Johnson
Margaret Hamilton
q.why: She wrote notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine.

q.q: Who led the team that wrote the on-board flight software for the Apollo Moon missions?
o: Margaret Hamilton
Ada Lovelace
Karen Spärck Jones
Grace Hopper
q.why: Margaret Hamilton led the Apollo flight software team.

q.q: Why can a lack of diversity make an AI system worse?
o: AI must be switched on by people of every age
Diverse teams always write shorter code
AI only works when built by large teams
AI trained on data from one group can work badly for others
q.why: Unrepresentative data can lead to biased results.

q.q: Which statement is a myth about computing?
o: Tech work involves a lot of teamwork
Women have shaped computing from the start
You must be a maths genius to work in tech
Many people first learn to code at school
q.why: Problem solving and practice matter more than genius.

q.q: What does SMART stand for?
o: Simple, Modern, Accurate, Reliable, Tested
Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
Specific, Meaningful, Ambitious, Real, Technical
Short, Measurable, Agreed, Realistic, Tidy
q.why: SMART targets are clear and have a deadline.

q.q: Which target is SMART?
o: Attend coding club every week until June
Get better at coding
Do more computer stuff
Be good at Digital Technology
q.why: It is specific, measurable and time-bound.

q.q: What is wrong with the target 'Learn about cyber security'?
o: It is too specific and measurable
Cyber security is not a real career
It has a deadline that is too short
It is not specific or measurable and has no deadline
q.why: A SMART version would name tasks and a date.

q.q: What is work experience?
o: A full-time permanent job with a salary
An exam taken at the end of Year 12
Time in a real workplace to see what a job is like
A website that lists local job adverts
q.why: It lets you try a job before choosing it.

q.q: How often should you review your careers plan?
o: Never, because it is fixed once written
At least once a year and when your interests change
Only after you finish university
Every day, changing it each time
q.why: Plans should change as you learn more.

q.q: Who can a pupil in NI talk to for impartial careers guidance?
o: A Careers Service adviser
An exam board moderator
A social media influencer
A website's terms and conditions
q.why: The Careers Service is part of the Department for the Economy.

q.q: Which is the best first step in making a careers plan?
o: Choose a job title and never consider anything else
Pick whichever subjects your friends choose
Apply for jobs before choosing your GCSEs
Think about what you enjoy and what you are good at
q.why: Knowing yourself comes before exploring options.

q.q: Which GCSE advice best keeps tech routes open?
o: Drop every subject except Digital Technology
Avoid maths because tech jobs never use it
Choose subjects you enjoy and are good at, including maths
Choose only the subjects that have the shortest exams
q.why: A balanced set of subjects you enjoy keeps many options open.
